propositions: The s3 optional extra must be declared in pyproject.toml with git-remote-s3>=0.3.2 as a dependency, following the existing optional-dependency pattern used by mcp and agents extras.

A require_s3_helper() function must probe both PATH availability (git-remote-s3 console script) and distribution version metadata, raising OptionalDependencyError with install instructions if either check fails.

The version comparison logic must parse leading numeric components of semantic version strings (splitting on dots and extracting integer prefixes) and compare them to (0, 3, 2), treating unparseable or missing versions as failures.

_optional.py must remain stdlib-only (no packaging or git_remote_s3 imports) and reuse the existing EXTRAS probe pattern so that guard_import('git_remote_s3', extra='s3') produces consistent missing-extra messaging.

Unit tests must cover happy path (script present, version 0.3.2), failures (script missing, metadata missing, version too old), and edge cases (suffixed versions like 0.3.2.post1, unparseable versions) via monkeypatching shutil.which and importlib.metadata.version.

The IfNoneMatch per-ref lock required to prevent multiple-bundles corruption is present in git-remote-s3 0.3.2+; the version guard ensures only safe versions are accepted for S3 ticket-store operations.
